books.section: The New Left, Feminism, and the Counterculture

source: original; stimulus is a licensed photograph viewed before writing (see figures) with an original account drawn from the grounding books

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: The Beatles, 1964, by Bernard Gotfryd, public domain, via the Library of Congress and Wikimedia Commons. Audience figure verified against Smithsonian Magazine and the National Portrait Gallery.
stimulus.text:
The photograph, taken in 1964, shows the four members of the Beatles — John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr — in four studio portraits against a gold curtain. All four wear dark suits and have the same mop-top haircut, with hair combed forward over their foreheads.

The Beatles first appeared on The Ed Sullivan Show on February 9, 1964. About 73 million Americans watched, the largest television audience to that date. Their appearance launched Beatlemania in the United States and opened the way for other British bands, a wave called the British Invasion.

stem: The backlash against the Beatles in the United States best shows which of the following?

options.text: Adults saw the band’s style as a challenge to traditional values
Most teenagers rejected the Beatles as too old-fashioned
options.misconception: Background: Teenagers were the Beatles’ biggest fans, not their rejecters.

options.text: Radio stations refused to play any British music
options.misconception: Background: British bands filled American radio after 1964.

options.text: The Beatles’ records sold poorly in the United States after 1964
options.misconception: Background: Their records topped the American charts.

rationales.A: Background: Conservatives were troubled by the Beatles’ long hair, hints of drug use, interest in Eastern religions, and challenges to traditional propriety.
rationales.B: Background: The passage says their appearance launched Beatlemania, a large following among young Americans.
rationales.C: Background: British bands filled American radio after 1964. Stations did not refuse them.
rationales.D: Background: Their records topped the American charts; ‘I Want to Hold Your Hand’ reached number one before they arrived.
rationales.general:
1. The Beatles arrived with mop-top hair, matching suits, and a new sound.
2. Background: Conservatives were troubled by their hair, hints of drug use, interest in Eastern religions, and challenges to traditional propriety.
3. That worry was not about music alone: it was about the values the look stood for.
4. A backlash against a look is a sign of a generation gap.
Remember: When adults attack a style, they are often defending the values behind it.
